question:
Choose a word that is similar in meaning to the word in bold.

It is inevitable that mistakes will occasionally occur.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Unavoidable.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Inevitable means certain to happen; unavoidable. (अपरिहार्य / अवश्यंभावी)

 

• 'It is inevitable that mistakes will occasionally occur' = mistakes cannot be avoided; they are bound to happen.
◦  Example: Change is inevitable in life.

 

• Prefix 'in-' (not) + 'evitable' (avoidable, from Latin 'evitare' = to avoid).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (Avertible): 'Avertible' means capable of being prevented — the opposite of inevitable.

 

• Option 2 (Avoidable): 'Avoidable' means able to be avoided — an antonym.

 

• Option 3 (Doubtful): 'Doubtful' means uncertain — inevitable implies certainty, not doubt.

 

• Synonyms of inevitable: unavoidable, inescapable, certain, sure, bound to happen, ineluctable. Antonyms: avoidable, preventable, uncertain, doubtful.

 

NOTE

 

• Related word: inevitability (noun). Do not confuse with 'inimitable' (impossible to copy).

question:
Choose a word similar in meaning to the underlined word.

The woman looked wan and fragile.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Pallid.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Wan (adjective) means (of a person's complexion) pale and giving the impression of illness or exhaustion. (पीला / मुरझाया हुआ)

 

• Pallid also means pale, typically because of poor health — an exact synonym.
◦  The word 'fragile' in the sentence supports the idea of weakness and paleness.

 

• Example: After the long illness, she looked wan and pallid.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (Flushed): 'Flushed' means red in the face (from heat, fever or embarrassment) — opposite of pale.

 

• Option 3 (Agile): 'Agile' means able to move quickly and easily — unrelated to complexion.

 

• Option 4 (Blooming): 'Blooming' means healthy and fresh-looking — the opposite of wan.

 

• Synonyms of wan: pale, pallid, ashen, pasty, sallow, colourless. Antonyms: rosy, ruddy, flushed, glowing, healthy.

 

NOTE

 

• Related words: pallor (noun: unhealthy pale appearance), sallow (yellowish, unhealthy skin).

question: What is the synonym of "Conceal"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Hide.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Conceal means to keep something secret or hide it from view. (छिपाना)

 

• Example: He tried to conceal his feelings.
◦  'Hide' is the exact synonym.

 

• Noun form: concealment.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (Reveal): 'Reveal' means to make known — an antonym.

 

• Option 3 (Display): 'Display' means to show openly — an antonym.

 

• Option 4 (Expose): 'Expose' means to uncover or make visible — an antonym.

 

• Synonyms of conceal: hide, cover, mask, veil, camouflage, suppress. Antonyms: reveal, disclose, expose, display, divulge.

 

NOTE

 

• Legal usage: 'concealment of facts' means hiding material information deliberately.

question:
Choose the word which has the opposite meaning to the given word :

QUARANTINED
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. liberty.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Quarantined means kept in isolation to prevent the spread of disease; confined or separated. (संगरोध / अलग-थलग रखा गया)

 

• Its opposite idea is liberty — the state of being free from confinement or restriction.
◦  Among the options, only 'liberty' conveys freedom; the others mean isolated.

 

• Example: After fourteen days of quarantine, the travellers regained their liberty.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (secluded): 'Secluded' means isolated, hidden away — a synonym.

 

• Option 3 (cloistered): 'Cloistered' means kept away from the outside world (like a monastery) — a synonym.

 

• Option 4 (isolated): 'Isolated' means set apart from others — a synonym.

 

• Word origin: 'Quarantine' comes from Italian 'quaranta giorni' (forty days) — the period ships were kept isolated in 14th-century Venice.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Liberty' is a noun while 'quarantined' is an adjective; SSC antonym questions sometimes pair different parts of speech — choose the option with the opposite meaning.

question:
Choose the correct antonym for the word highlighted in bold.

She approached her new project with great zeal and enthusiasm.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Indifference.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Zeal means great energy or enthusiasm in pursuit of a cause or objective. (उत्साह / जोश)

 

• Its antonym is Indifference — lack of interest, concern or enthusiasm.
◦  Example: She approached the project with zeal, not indifference.

 

• Option 1 is the only option opposite in meaning.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (Passion): 'Passion' is a synonym of zeal.

 

• Option 3 (Enthusiasm): 'Enthusiasm' is a synonym (also used in the sentence itself).

 

• Option 4 (Energy): 'Energy' is similar in meaning to zeal.

 

• Synonyms of zeal: ardour, fervour, passion, eagerness, zest. Antonyms: apathy, indifference, lethargy, unconcern.

 

NOTE

 

• Related words: zealous (adj.), zealot (a fanatical person).

question:
Choose the one word substitute for the below sentence.

Manish's approach was unique, representing a clear departure from the standard norms usually followed.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Anomaly.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• An anomaly is something that deviates from what is standard, normal or expected. (असामान्यता / विसंगति)

 

• 'representing a clear departure from the standard norms usually followed' = an anomaly.
◦  Example: The result was an anomaly in the data.

 

• Option 2 is the one-word substitute.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (Uniformity): 'Uniformity' means sameness — the opposite of departure from norms.

 

• Option 3 (Conformity): 'Conformity' means following accepted rules or standards — the opposite.

 

• Option 4 (Regularity): 'Regularity' means following a fixed pattern — the opposite.

 

• Related words: anomalous (adj.), aberration (a departure from what is normal), deviation, irregularity.

 

NOTE

 

• Greek 'an-' (not) + 'homalos' (even) — 'uneven, irregular'.

question:
Identify the grammatical error in the sentence below.

There isn't much time to spare. You'd better buy your ticket with the train.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. with the train.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• We buy a ticket for a train (or 'a train ticket'); the preposition 'with' is wrong. (के लिए)

 

• Correct: "You'd better buy your ticket for the train."
◦  Hence the error lies in 'with the train'.

 

• 'You'd better' (= you had better) + base verb (buy) is correct.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (isn't much): 'isn't much' is correct with the uncountable noun 'time'.

 

• Option 2 (time to spare): 'time to spare' is a correct idiomatic phrase (free time available).

 

• Option 3 (buy your ticket): 'buy your ticket' is correct; 'had better' is followed by the bare infinitive.

 

• Had better: had better + V1 (You had better leave now); negative: had better not + V1.

 

NOTE

 

• Use 'much' with uncountable nouns (much time, much water) and 'many' with countable nouns (many tickets).

question:
Identify the grammatical error in the sentence below.

The person with who Maya shared the flat had not paid his rent.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. who Maya shared the flat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• After a preposition (with), the objective form whom must be used, not 'who'. (कर्म रूप सर्वनाम)

 

• Correct: "The person with whom Maya shared the flat had not paid his rent."
◦  Hence the error is in 'who Maya shared the flat'.

 

• Test: Maya shared the flat with him → him = whom.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (person with): 'person with' is correct; the preposition itself is fine.

 

• Option 3 (his rent): 'his rent' is correct; the possessive agrees with 'the person'.

 

• Option 4 (had not paid): 'had not paid' is correct past perfect.

 

• Who vs Whom: who = subject; whom = object or after a preposition (to whom, with whom, for whom).

 

NOTE

 

• In informal English, 'who Maya shared the flat with' is heard, but in formal/exam English 'with whom' is required.

question: Identify the incorrect sentence.
option_1: Did they sent me any books for preparation of examination.
option_2: Reactions to the annual play have been favorable.
option_3: The author of the stories in these books is Mary Gomes.
option_4: Many lines in the poem are especially good.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Did they sent me any books for preparation of examination.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• After the auxiliary 'did', the base form (V1) of the verb is used. 'Did they sent' is wrong; it should be 'Did they send'. (सहायक क्रिया के बाद V1)

 

• Also, a question should end with a question mark, not a full stop.
◦  Correct: "Did they send me any books for preparation of examination?"

 

• Hence the sentence in Option 1 is incorrect.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (Reactions to the annual play have been favorable): "Reactions to the annual play have been favorable." – correct: plural subject 'Reactions' with 'have been'.

 

• Option 3 (The author of the stories in these books is Mary Gomes): "The author of the stories in these books is Mary Gomes." – correct: the subject is 'The author' (singular), so 'is'.

 

• Option 4 (Many lines in the poem are especially good): "Many lines in the poem are especially good." – correct: plural subject 'Many lines' with 'are'.

 

• Rule: do/does/did + V1 (base form) — Did he go? He does not know. She did not come.

 

NOTE

 

• In subject–verb agreement, the verb agrees with the head noun, not with nouns inside a prepositional phrase ('of the stories', 'in the poem').

question: Identify the incorrect sentence.
option_1: All of the cities in California can to be affected by the rain yesterday.
option_2: Seven people were rescued from the fire yesterday.
option_3: Half of the boxes are empty as the children have eaten the chocolates.
option_4: Each packet can have a variable number of chocolates.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. All of the cities in California can to be affected by the rain yesterday.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A modal verb (can) is followed by the bare infinitive (without 'to'). 'can to be affected' is wrong. (Modal + V1)

 

• Moreover, 'can' does not suit a past event ('yesterday'); the correct sentence would be "All of the cities in California were affected / could have been affected by the rain yesterday."
◦  Hence Option 1 is incorrect.

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4 are grammatically correct.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (Seven people were rescued from the fire yesterday): "Seven people were rescued from the fire yesterday." – correct simple past passive.

 

• Option 3 (Half of the boxes are empty as the children have eaten the chocolates): "Half of the boxes are empty…" – correct: 'Half of' + plural noun takes a plural verb.

 

• Option 4 (Each packet can have a variable number of chocolates): "Each packet can have a variable number of chocolates." – correct: 'Each' takes a singular noun and verb; 'can have' is correct.

 

• Modals: can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would, must + V1 (no 'to'). Exceptions: ought to, have to, used to.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Half of / Part of / Most of / All of' take the verb according to the noun that follows: Half of the cake is eaten; Half of the boxes are empty.

question:
Choose the best option to replace the underlined part to improve the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution.'

The suspect is currently under custody while the police continue their investigation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. in custody.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct idiom is in custody — held by the police or under legal detention. (हिरासत में)

 

• Correct: "The suspect is currently in custody while the police continue their investigation."
◦  'Take someone into custody' = arrest.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (at custody): 'at custody' is not idiomatic.

 

• Option 3 (on custody): 'on custody' is not idiomatic.

 

• Option 4 (No substitution): 'No substitution' is wrong because 'under custody' is non-standard; standard English uses 'in custody'.

 

• Related phrases: in custody (detained); take into custody (arrest); judicial custody (in jail on court's order); police custody (held by police); custody of a child (legal guardianship).

 

NOTE

 

• 'Under arrest' is correct, but 'under custody' is not — a common SSC trap.

question:
Choose the best option to replace the underlined part to improve the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution.'

He needs to get on off his work if he wants to finish on time.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Get on with.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The phrasal verb get on with means to continue or make progress with a task. (काम जारी रखना)

 

• Correct: "He needs to get on with his work if he wants to finish on time."
◦  'get on off' is meaningless.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (Get on from): 'Get on from' is not a standard phrasal verb.

 

• Option 2 (Get on for): 'Get on for' means approaching a time/age (It's getting on for midnight) — does not fit here.

 

• Option 4 (No substitution): 'No substitution' is wrong since 'get on off' is incorrect.

 

• Other phrasal verbs with 'get': get on with someone (have a good relationship); get over (recover); get through (pass); get along (manage); get by (survive with little).

 

NOTE

 

• 'Get on with it!' is also used informally to tell someone to hurry up.

question:
In the given passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage intently and choose the most appropriate option to fill in each blank:

Education is usually seen as the pillar of a successful society. It provides people with the necessary information and skills to advance their lives and serve their communities. Apart from studies, education develops critical thinking and (1)________, making people analyse issues and make sound decisions.

 

One of the difficulties with education today is achieving equal access for everyone. Socioeconomic inequality tends to form obstacles, leaving disadvantaged groups lacking resources. To address this, investment must be made in infrastructure and (2)________ policies that are focused on inclusivity.

 

Technology has also revolutionized education, and learning has become more accessible with the help of online platforms. This change brings concerns regarding the (3)________ of typical classroom experiences, which focus on direct interaction and collaboration.

 

Finally, learning is not simply the process of gaining knowledge; it's about the molding of values and instilling a sense of (4)________. By giving equal weight to academic success and social responsibility, societies can build a future that is both innovative and (5)________.

 

What should come in the place of blank number 1?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Creativity.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Blank (1) follows 'critical thinking and ___, making people analyse issues and make sound decisions'. The word must be a mental ability that pairs naturally with 'critical thinking'. Creativity — the ability to generate new ideas — is the standard pairing ('critical thinking and creativity'). (रचनात्मकता)

 

• The PDF key marks 'Memory', but memory is recall of information; it does not help people 'analyse issues'. Education is commonly described as developing 'critical thinking and creativity'.
◦  Hence, on verification, Creativity is the academically appropriate answer.

 

• The passage's opening lines also stress advancing lives and serving communities — higher-order skills, not rote recall.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (Memory): 'Memory' refers to storing and recalling information; the passage contrasts education with mere studies ('Apart from studies'), so rote memory is not what is meant.

 

• Option 3 (Physical strength): 'Physical strength' has no relation to analysing issues.

 

• Option 4 (Athletic ability): 'Athletic ability' is unrelated to decision-making.

 

• Collocation tip: critical thinking and creativity; problem-solving and decision-making; knowledge and skills.

 

NOTE

 

• In cloze tests, the blank should agree with the idea that follows it ('making people analyse issues') and with the word it is joined to by 'and' (critical thinking).

question:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence.

Take a pair of binoculars with you lest you all should miss the chance of looking at the distant scenes.
option_1: Let a pair of binoculars be taken with you lest the chance of looking at the distant scenes would missed by you all.
option_2: Let a pair of binoculars taken with you lest the chance of looking at the distant scenes should be missed by you all.
option_3: Let a pair of binoculars be taken with you otherwise the chance of looking at the distant scenes would be missed by you all.
option_4: Let a pair of binoculars be taken with you lest the chance of looking at the distant scenes should be missed by you all.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Let a pair of binoculars be taken with you lest the chance of looking at the distant scenes should be missed by you all.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The given sentence is an imperative with a lest clause. Imperative passive: Let + object + be + V3. The 'lest' clause takes should: 'lest … should be missed by you all'. (कर्मवाच्य – आज्ञार्थक वाक्य)

 

• Passive: "Let a pair of binoculars be taken with you lest the chance of looking at the distant scenes should be missed by you all."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (Let a pair of binoculars be taken with you lest the chance of looking at the distant scenes would missed by you all): 'would missed' is ungrammatical; after 'lest', 'should' is used, and 'be' is missing.

 

• Option 2 (Let a pair of binoculars taken with you lest the chance of looking at the distant scenes should be missed by you all): 'Let a pair of binoculars taken' – 'be' is missing after the object.

 

• Option 3 (Let a pair of binoculars be taken with you otherwise the chance of looking at the distant scenes would be missed by you all): Replaces 'lest' with 'otherwise' and 'should' with 'would' — changes the structure.

 

• Lest means 'for fear that / so that … not'. It is always followed by should (or the base verb); never use 'not' after lest.

 

NOTE

 

• Imperative passive patterns: Open the door → Let the door be opened. Don't insult the poor → Let the poor not be insulted.

The tiger ate all the flesh that the zoo-keeper had kept in the enclosure.
option_1: All the flesh that had been kept by the zoo-keeper in the enclosure was eaten by the tiger.
option_2: All the flesh that was kept by the zoo-keeper in the enclosure was eaten by the tiger.
option_3: All the flesh that had been kept by the zoo-keeper in the enclosure had been eaten by the tiger.
option_4: All the flesh that was kept by the zoo-keeper in the enclosure had been eaten by the tiger.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. All the flesh that had been kept by the zoo-keeper in the enclosure was eaten by the tiger.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The main clause is in the simple past (ate → was eaten) and the relative clause is in the past perfect (had kept → had been kept). Each clause keeps its own tense. (कर्मवाच्य)

 

• Passive: "All the flesh that had been kept by the zoo-keeper in the enclosure was eaten by the tiger."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (All the flesh that was kept by the zoo-keeper in the enclosure was eaten by the tiger): 'was kept' changes the past perfect of the relative clause to simple past.

 

• Option 3 (All the flesh that had been kept by the zoo-keeper in the enclosure had been eaten by the tiger): 'had been eaten' wrongly changes the main verb 'ate' to past perfect.

 

• Option 4 (All the flesh that was kept by the zoo-keeper in the enclosure had been eaten by the tiger): Both tenses are interchanged — wrong.

 

• Rule: In complex sentences, change each clause into the passive while retaining its original tense.

 

NOTE

 

• 'All the flesh' is uncountable, so it takes a singular verb (was).

question:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence.

The cheetah chased the wild boar with lightening speed.
option_1: The wild boar has been chased with lightening speed by the cheetah.
option_2: The wild boar was chased with lightening speed by the cheetah.
option_3: The wild boar had been chased with lightening speed by the cheetah.
option_4: The wild boar was being chased with lightening speed by the cheetah.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The wild boar was chased with lightening speed by the cheetah.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The active sentence is in the simple past tense (chased). Passive: Object + was/were + V3 + by + agent. (कर्मवाच्य)

 

• Passive: "The wild boar was chased with lightening speed by the cheetah."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (The wild boar has been chased with lightening speed by the cheetah): 'has been chased' is present perfect — wrong tense.

 

• Option 3 (The wild boar had been chased with lightening speed by the cheetah): 'had been chased' is past perfect — wrong tense.

 

• Option 4 (The wild boar was being chased with lightening speed by the cheetah): 'was being chased' is past continuous — wrong tense.

 

• Spelling note: The standard spelling is 'lightning speed' (lightning = flash in the sky); 'lightening' means making lighter. The question retains the source text as given.

 

NOTE

 

• Simple past passive: was/were + V3.

question:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence.

Suruchi exclaimed that the fish possessed a very big dorsal fin.
option_1: It was exclaimed by Suruchi that a very big dorsal fin was possessed by the fish.
option_2: It was exclaimed by Suruchi that a very big dorsal fin had been possessed by the fish.
option_3: Suruchi exclaimed that a very big dorsal fin is possessed by the fish.
option_4: It exclaimed Suruchi that a very big dorsal fin was possessed by the fish.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. It was exclaimed by Suruchi that a very big dorsal fin was possessed by the fish.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The active sentence is a complex sentence with a noun clause as the object of 'exclaimed'. It is changed using the introductory 'It': "It was exclaimed by Suruchi that…", and the noun clause is also changed to passive. (कर्मवाच्य – 'It' संरचना)

 

• Past tense 'possessed' → 'was possessed'.
◦  Passive: "It was exclaimed by Suruchi that a very big dorsal fin was possessed by the fish."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (It was exclaimed by Suruchi that a very big dorsal fin had been possessed by the fish): 'had been possessed' changes the simple past to past perfect.

 

• Option 3 (Suruchi exclaimed that a very big dorsal fin is possessed by the fish): Main clause is still active and 'is possessed' is the wrong tense.

 

• Option 4 (It exclaimed Suruchi that a very big dorsal fin was possessed by the fish): 'It exclaimed Suruchi' is ungrammatical — 'was … by' is missing.

 

• Pattern: People say that … → It is said that …; He announced that … → It was announced by him that …

 

NOTE

 

• The dorsal fin is the fin located on the back of a fish or whale.

question:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence.

The usher must have made the guests sit by the time the dinner was ready.
option_1: The guests must have been made sit by the usher by the time the dinner was ready.
option_2: The guests must have been made to sit by the usher by the time the dinner was ready.
option_3: The guests must have been made to sit by the usher by the time the dinner had been ready.
option_4: The guests must have made to sit by the usher by the time the dinner had been ready.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The guests must have been made to sit by the usher by the time the dinner was ready.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Verbs like make, let, see, hear take a bare infinitive in the active voice (made the guests sit), but in the passive voice 'to' is added: made to sit. (कर्मवाच्य – make + to)

 

• 'must have made' (modal perfect) → must have been made. The time clause 'by the time the dinner was ready' stays unchanged.
◦  Passive: "The guests must have been made to sit by the usher by the time the dinner was ready."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (The guests must have been made sit by the usher by the time the dinner was ready): 'made sit' — 'to' is missing in the passive.

 

• Option 3 (The guests must have been made to sit by the usher by the time the dinner had been ready): Changes the time clause 'was ready' to 'had been ready' — the dependent clause is not changed in voice conversion.

 

• Option 4 (The guests must have made to sit by the usher by the time the dinner had been ready): 'must have made to sit' — 'been' is missing, so it is not passive.

 

• Examples: They made him work. → He was made to work. I saw her dance. → She was seen to dance. (But: 'let' → be allowed to.)

 

NOTE

 

• Modal perfect passive: modal + have been + V3.

question:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Active Voice.

A table was reserved for the family at the restaurant.
option_1: They reserved a table for the family at the restaurant.
option_2: The family reserved a table for them at the restaurant.
option_3: The restaurant reserved a table for the family by them.
option_4: They were reserving a table for the family at the restaurant.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. They reserved a table for the family at the restaurant.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The passive sentence "A table was reserved for the family at the restaurant" has no agent. In the active voice, an indefinite subject like They/Someone is supplied. (कर्तृवाच्य)

 

• Simple past passive (was reserved) → simple past active (reserved).
◦  Active: "They reserved a table for the family at the restaurant."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (The family reserved a table for them at the restaurant): "The family reserved a table for them…" changes the meaning (the family becomes the doer, 'for them' is illogical).

 

• Option 3 (The restaurant reserved a table for the family by them): "The restaurant reserved … by them" mixes active and passive and is ungrammatical.

 

• Option 4 (They were reserving a table for the family at the restaurant): 'were reserving' is past continuous — wrong tense.

 

• Agentless passive → active: use they, someone, people, one or we as the subject.

 

NOTE

 

• Never make the beneficiary (for the family) the subject unless the sentence says so.

question:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Active Voice.

The cake was decorated by the children for the party.
option_1: The children decorated the cake for the party.
option_2: The children were decorating the cake for the party.
option_3: The children decorate the cake for the party.
option_4: The cake decorated the children for the party.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. The children decorated the cake for the party.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The passive sentence is in the simple past (was decorated). In active voice: Subject (agent) + V2 + object. (कर्तृवाच्य)

 

• Active: "The children decorated the cake for the party."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (The children were decorating the cake for the party): 'were decorating' is past continuous — wrong tense.

 

• Option 3 (The children decorate the cake for the party): 'decorate' is simple present — wrong tense.

 

• Option 4 (The cake decorated the children for the party): 'The cake decorated the children' reverses the roles and is absurd.

 

• Simple past: Active – V2; Passive – was/were + V3.

 

NOTE

 

• The phrase 'for the party' (purpose) remains unchanged.

question:
Choose the correct indirect narration of the following statement from the given alternatives:

Riyaz said, "I will be there by tomorrow morning."
option_1: Riyaz said that he would be there by tomorrow morning.
option_2: Riyaz said that he will be there by the following morning.
option_3: Riyaz said that he will be there by tomorrow morning.
option_4: Riyaz said that he would be there by the following morning.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Riyaz said that he would be there by the following morning.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• With a past reporting verb (said): I → he, will → would, tomorrow morning → the following morning (the next morning). (अप्रत्यक्ष कथन)

 

• Indirect: "Riyaz said that he would be there by the following morning."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (Riyaz said that he would be there by tomorrow morning): 'tomorrow morning' is not changed to 'the following morning'.

 

• Option 2 (Riyaz said that he will be there by the following morning): 'will' is not changed to 'would'.

 

• Option 3 (Riyaz said that he will be there by tomorrow morning): Neither 'will' nor 'tomorrow' is changed.

 

• Time/place changes: tomorrow → the next day/the following day; today → that day; now → then; here → there; ago → before; this → that.

 

NOTE

 

• 'here' → 'there' is common, but since the direct speech already uses 'there', it stays unchanged.

question:
Choose the correct indirect narration of the following statement from the given alternatives:

William said to Margaret, "You are now twenty-one years old and you cannot behave like a child."
option_1: William told Margaret that she was then twenty-one years old and she could not behave like a child.
option_2: William told Margaret that she is then twenty-one years old and she could not behave like a child.
option_3: William told Margaret that she is now twenty-one years old and she could not behave like a child.
option_4: William told Margaret that she was now twenty-one years old and she could not behave like a child.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. William told Margaret that she was then twenty-one years old and she could not behave like a child.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• With the past reporting verb 'said to' → told; You → she, are → was, now → then, cannot → could not. (अप्रत्यक्ष कथन)

 

• Indirect: "William told Margaret that she was then twenty-one years old and she could not behave like a child."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (William told Margaret that she is then twenty-one years old and she could not behave like a child): 'is' is not backshifted to 'was'.

 

• Option 3 (William told Margaret that she is now twenty-one years old and she could not behave like a child): Neither 'is' nor 'now' is changed.

 

• Option 4 (William told Margaret that she was now twenty-one years old and she could not behave like a child): 'now' is not changed to 'then'.

 

• Reporting verb: 'said to + person' becomes 'told + person' for statements.

 

NOTE

 

• When a sentence has two coordinate clauses joined by 'and', 'that' may be repeated (and that she could not…), though it is often omitted.

question:
Choose the correct indirect narration of the following statement from the given alternatives:

The trainer said to the trainees, “Go on writing this paragraph till you understand it very clearly."
option_1: The trainer asked the trainees going on writing that paragraph till they understood it very clearly.
option_2: The trainer asked the trainees to go on writing that paragraph till they understood it very clearly.
option_3: The trainer asked the trainees to go on writing that paragraph till they understand it very clearly.
option_4: The trainer asked the trainees to went on writing that paragraph till they understood it very clearly.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The trainer asked the trainees to go on writing that paragraph till they understood it very clearly.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• An imperative (command/instruction) is reported with asked/told/ordered + object + to-infinitive. (आज्ञार्थक वाक्य – अप्रत्यक्ष कथन)

 

• 'Go on writing' → to go on writing; this → that; you understand → they understood.
◦  Indirect: "The trainer asked the trainees to go on writing that paragraph till they understood it very clearly."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (The trainer asked the trainees going on writing that paragraph till they understood it very clearly): 'going on writing' — the to-infinitive is required after 'asked the trainees'.

 

• Option 3 (The trainer asked the trainees to go on writing that paragraph till they understand it very clearly): 'understand' is not backshifted to 'understood'.

 

• Option 4 (The trainer asked the trainees to went on writing that paragraph till they understood it very clearly): 'to went' is ungrammatical; the infinitive is 'to + V1'.

 

• Reporting verbs for imperatives: order, command, request, advise, urge, forbid, ask, tell + object + to-infinitive.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Go on + V-ing' means continue doing something.

question:
Choose the most suitable preposition from the given options to fill in the blank in the following sentence.

The incident caused a rift _____ the two best friends.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. between.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Between is used for two persons or things; among for more than two. (दो के बीच)

 

• "The incident caused a rift between the two best friends." — 'two' clearly indicates 'between'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (among): 'among' is used for more than two.

 

• Option 3 (for): 'a rift for' is not idiomatic.

 

• Option 4 (in): 'a rift in' is used with a group or thing (a rift in the party), not between two individuals.

 

• Rift = a serious break in friendly relations. Collocations: a rift between/with someone; a rift in a group.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Between' can also be used for more than two when referring to individual relations: a treaty between three nations.

question:
The following sentence has two blanks. Choose the most suitable set of prepositions from the given options to fill in the blanks and complete the sentence meaningfully.

The poor fellow fell _____ his bicycle and landed _____ a puddle.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. off, in.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• One falls off a bicycle/horse/ladder (movement away from a surface) and lands in a puddle (enclosed by water). (से गिरना / में गिरना)

 

• "The poor fellow fell off his bicycle and landed in a puddle."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (from, into): 'fell from his bicycle' is acceptable in some usage, but 'fell off' is the standard idiom; 'landed into' is incorrect — 'land in' is used.

 

• Option 3 (down, to): 'fell down his bicycle' and 'landed to a puddle' are both incorrect.

 

• Option 4 (of, at): 'fell of' (of ≠ off) and 'landed at a puddle' are incorrect.

 

• Off vs Of: off = away from a surface (fall off, get off); of = belonging/relationship (a cup of tea).

 

NOTE

 

• Land in (water, trouble, jail); land on (a surface); land at (an airport).

question:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Direct Speech.

The teacher reminded the students to submit their assignments by Friday.
option_1: The teacher said to the students, "Your assignments must be submitted by Friday."
option_2: The teacher reminded, "You have to submit your assignments by Friday."
option_3: The teacher reminded the students, "Submit your assignments by Friday."
option_4: The teacher said to the students, "You should submitted your assignments by Friday."
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. The teacher reminded the students, "Submit your assignments by Friday."

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The indirect sentence uses reminded + object + to-infinitive, which reports an imperative (an instruction). In direct speech it becomes an imperative sentence: "Submit your assignments by Friday." (प्रत्यक्ष कथन – आज्ञार्थक)

 

• The reporting verb 'reminded' and the listener 'the students' are retained; 'their' → 'your'.
◦  Direct: The teacher reminded the students, "Submit your assignments by Friday."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (The teacher said to the students, "Your assignments must be submitted by Friday."): Changes the imperative into a passive statement with 'must be submitted' — not a faithful conversion.

 

• Option 2 (The teacher reminded, "You have to submit your assignments by Friday."): 'reminded' without the object (the students) is incomplete; 'You have to submit' is a statement, not an imperative.

 

• Option 4 (The teacher said to the students, "You should submitted your assignments by Friday."): 'should submitted' is ungrammatical (should + V1).

 

• Indirect → direct (imperatives): asked/told/ordered/reminded + object + to V1 → "V1 …" (imperative).

 

NOTE

 

• In direct speech, possessive pronouns referring to the listener become second person (their → your).

question:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Direct Speech.

He said that he had been waiting for that opportunity for years.
option_1: He said, "I have been waiting for the opportunity for years."
option_2: He said, "I am waiting for that opportunity for years."
option_3: He said, "I have been waiting for this opportunity for years."
option_4: He said, "I waited for that opportunity for years."
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. He said, "I have been waiting for this opportunity for years."

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Reversing indirect to direct: he → I, had been waiting → have been waiting (past perfect continuous → present perfect continuous), that → this. (प्रत्यक्ष कथन)

 

• Direct: He said, "I have been waiting for this opportunity for years."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (He said, "I have been waiting for the opportunity for years."): Uses 'the opportunity' — 'that' should be restored to 'this', not 'the'.

 

• Option 2 (He said, "I am waiting for that opportunity for years."): 'I am waiting … for years' is ungrammatical; with 'for years', the perfect continuous is required.

 

• Option 4 (He said, "I waited for that opportunity for years."): 'I waited for that opportunity' changes the tense and keeps 'that'.

 

• Reverse changes: past perfect → present perfect/simple past; that → this; there → here; then → now.

 

NOTE

 

• Present perfect continuous (have been + V-ing) + for/since shows an action continuing up to now.

question:
Change the following sentence into the Active form.

The construction of the skyscraper is scheduled to have been completed by the end of the year.
option_1: The skyscraper will have completed the construction by the end of the year.
option_2: They are scheduling to have completed the construction of the skyscraper by the end of the year.
option_3: The construction of the skyscraper will be completed by the end of the year.
option_4: They are scheduled to complete the construction of the skyscraper by the end of the year.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. They are scheduled to complete the construction of the skyscraper by the end of the year.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The passive infinitive 'to have been completed' becomes the active infinitive 'to complete', and an indefinite subject They is supplied for the agentless passive. (कर्तृवाच्य)

 

• Active: "They are scheduled to complete the construction of the skyscraper by the end of the year."
◦  'are scheduled' is retained as the time-arrangement phrase.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (The skyscraper will have completed the construction by the end of the year): 'The skyscraper will have completed the construction' makes the building the doer — illogical.

 

• Option 2 (They are scheduling to have completed the construction of the skyscraper by the end of the year): 'They are scheduling to have completed' is ungrammatical and changes the meaning (scheduling ≠ scheduled).

 

• Option 3 (The construction of the skyscraper will be completed by the end of the year): It is still in the passive voice.

 

• Infinitive voice: to + V1 (active) ↔ to be + V3 (passive); to have + V3 (perfect active) ↔ to have been + V3 (perfect passive).

 

NOTE

 

• 'be scheduled to' = be planned to happen at a particular time.

question:
Choose the most suitable preposition from the given options to fill in the blank in the following sentence:

The footfall has gone up _____ ten percent.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. by.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The preposition by is used to express the amount or degree of difference in an increase or decrease. (के द्वारा / की मात्रा में)

 

• "The footfall has gone up by ten percent."
◦  Similarly: Prices rose by 5%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (with): 'gone up with' is not idiomatic.

 

• Option 2 (for): 'gone up for ten percent' is incorrect.

 

• Option 4 (of): 'gone up of ten percent' is incorrect; 'of' is used with nouns: 'an increase of 10%'.

 

• Rule: Verb + by + amount (increase by, reduce by, win by); Noun + of + amount (an increase of, a rise of).

 

NOTE

 

• 'Footfall' = the number of people entering a place (shop, event) in a given time.

question:
Change the following sentence into the Active form.

The new theory is said to have been developed over decades.
option_1: They say that the new theory has been developed over decades.
option_2: They say that the new theory was developed over decades.
option_3: Someone is said to have developed the new theory over decades.
option_4: The new theory developed over decades.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. They say that the new theory has been developed over decades.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 'is said to have been developed' is an impersonal passive. Its active form is They say that + a clause. The perfect infinitive 'to have been developed' refers to an action earlier than 'say', and with the duration 'over decades' the present perfect 'has been developed' fits. (कर्तृवाच्य – They say that)

 

• Active: "They say that the new theory has been developed over decades."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (They say that the new theory was developed over decades): 'was developed over decades' — simple past does not match 'over decades' continuing to the present as well as the present perfect does.

 

• Option 3 (Someone is said to have developed the new theory over decades): 'Someone is said to have developed…' is still passive ('is said').

 

• Option 4 (The new theory developed over decades): 'The new theory developed over decades' removes the reporting element 'is said'.

 

• Pattern: He is said to be rich. → They say that he is rich. He is said to have been rich. → They say that he was/has been rich.

 

NOTE

 

• In such sentences the reporting verb (say, believe, think) becomes active with 'They/People' as the subject.

question:
Change the following sentence into the Active form.

The decision will have been announced before the meeting concludes.
option_1: Someone was announced the decision before the meeting concludes.
option_2: They will have announced the decision before the meeting concludes.
option_3: The decision will be announced before the meeting concludes.
option_4: The meeting will have announced the decision.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. They will have announced the decision before the meeting concludes.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The passive sentence is in the future perfect tense (will have been announced). The active form is will have + V3; an indefinite subject They is supplied. (कर्तृवाच्य)

 

• Active: "They will have announced the decision before the meeting concludes."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (Someone was announced the decision before the meeting concludes): 'Someone was announced the decision' is ungrammatical and in the wrong tense.

 

• Option 3 (The decision will be announced before the meeting concludes): It is still in the passive voice (will be announced).

 

• Option 4 (The meeting will have announced the decision): 'The meeting will have announced the decision' makes the meeting the doer and drops 'before the meeting concludes'.

 

• Future perfect: Active – will have + V3; Passive – will have been + V3.

 

NOTE

 

• The time clause 'before the meeting concludes' remains unchanged in voice conversion.

question:
Choose the most suitable preposition from the given options to fill in the blank in the following sentence:

She took the job _____ her parents’ wishes.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. against.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom is against someone's wishes — contrary to what someone wants. (इच्छा के विरुद्ध)

 

• "She took the job against her parents' wishes."
◦  'Against somebody's wishes/advice/will' is the standard collocation.

 

• Since the question asks for the most suitable preposition, the fixed collocation against … wishes is the best answer.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (despite): 'despite her parents' wishes' is also grammatically possible, but the fixed collocation used with 'wishes' is 'against'; the question asks for the most suitable preposition.

 

• Option 2 (without): 'without her parents' wishes' is not idiomatic.

 

• Option 3 (inspite): 'inspite' is a misspelling; the correct form is 'in spite of' (three words, followed by 'of').

 

• Despite vs In spite of: despite + noun (no 'of'); in spite of + noun. 'Despite of' is always wrong.

 

NOTE

 

• Collocations with 'against': against one's will, against the law, against the odds, against all advice.

question:
The following sentence has two blanks. Choose the most suitable set of prepositions from the given options to fill in the blanks and complete the sentence meaningfully:

The manager was alarmed _____ the delay and dissatisfied _____ the final outcome.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. at, with.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The adjective alarmed takes at (or by), and dissatisfied takes with. (पर चिंतित / से असंतुष्ट)

 

• "The manager was alarmed at the delay and dissatisfied with the final outcome."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (by, with): 'by, with' — 'alarmed by' is also used in modern English, but traditional grammar (Wren & Martin) prescribes 'alarmed at'; hence 'at, with' is the best answer.

 

• Option 2 (at, about): 'dissatisfied about' is not the standard preposition; it takes 'with'.

 

• Option 4 (for, by): 'alarmed for' and 'dissatisfied by' are both incorrect.

 

• Adjective + preposition: satisfied/dissatisfied with; surprised at; angry with (person)/at (thing); disappointed with/in; afraid of.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Alarmed at the news' = frightened or worried by the news.

question:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Direct Speech.

The professor admitted that he had never delivered a lecture on that particular topic in any of his classes.
option_1: The professor said, “I’ve never delivered a lecture on this particular topic in any of my classes.”
option_2: The professor admitted, “I’d never delivered a lecture on this particular topic in any class.”
option_3: The professor admitted, “I have not deliver a lecture on that particular topic in any of my classes.”
option_4: The professor said, “I have never delivered a lecture on this particular topic in none of my classes.”
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. The professor said, “I’ve never delivered a lecture on this particular topic in any of my classes.”

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Reversing indirect to direct: 'admitted that' can be shown as said; he → I, had never delivered → have never delivered ('I've'), that → this, his → my. (प्रत्यक्ष कथन)

 

• Direct: The professor said, "I've never delivered a lecture on this particular topic in any of my classes."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (The professor admitted, “I’d never delivered a lecture on this particular topic in any class.”): 'I'd never delivered' retains the past perfect, and 'in any class' drops 'of my classes'.

 

• Option 3 (The professor admitted, “I have not deliver a lecture on that particular topic in any of my classes.”): 'have not deliver' is ungrammatical (have + V3) and 'that' is not restored to 'this'.

 

• Option 4 (The professor said, “I have never delivered a lecture on this particular topic in none of my classes.”): 'never … in none of my classes' is a double negative — incorrect.

 

• Double negative rule: Use only one negative word in a clause: never … any (not never … none).

 

NOTE

 

• "I've" = I have; "I'd" = I had / I would.

question:
Which word is nearest in meaning to 'demonstrating'?

This trend is already booming in China, demonstrating significant potential globally.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Showcasing.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Demonstrating here means showing clearly or displaying something to others. In the context 'demonstrating significant potential globally', Showcasing (displaying something to advantage) is the nearest in meaning. (प्रदर्शित करना)

 

• The trend 'is already booming in China', thereby showcasing its potential to the world.
◦  The PDF key gives 'Showcasing'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (Exhibiting): 'Exhibiting' means publicly displaying (objects, symptoms) — close, but usually used for displays of art or signs of a condition.

 

• Option 2 (Displaying): 'Displaying' means showing visibly — close in meaning, but 'showcasing' better conveys presenting something favourably to a wide audience.

 

• Option 4 (Revealing): 'Revealing' means making known something previously hidden — not the sense here.

 

• Synonyms of demonstrate: show, showcase, display, exhibit, illustrate, prove, manifest.

 

NOTE

 

• When several options look similar, choose the one that best fits the context of the sentence (here: presenting potential to the world).

question: What is the antonym of "Copious"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Meager.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Copious means abundant; in large quantities. (प्रचुर / भरपूर)

 

• Its antonym is Meager (meagre) — lacking in quantity or quality; scanty.
◦  Example: She took copious notes; his salary was meagre.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (Plentiful): 'Plentiful' is a synonym of copious.

 

• Option 3 (Ample): 'Ample' (enough or more than enough) is a synonym.

 

• Option 4 (Overflowing): 'Overflowing' (filled beyond capacity) is similar in meaning.

 

• Synonyms of copious: abundant, profuse, plentiful, lavish, bountiful. Antonyms: meagre, scanty, sparse, scarce, paltry.

 

NOTE

 

• British spelling: meagre; American spelling: meager.

question: What is the antonym of "Irascible"?

• Option 3 (Hostile): 'Hostile' (unfriendly, antagonistic) is similar in sense.

 

• Option 4 (Fractious): 'Fractious' (irritable, quarrelsome) is a synonym.

 

• Synonyms of irascible: irritable, testy, touchy, choleric, cantankerous. Antonyms: calm, placid, tranquil, easy-going, even-tempered.

 

NOTE

 

• Latin 'ira' = anger (also in 'ire', 'irate').

question:
Which word can best replace 'moored' in this context?

The boat was moored at the edge of the island.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Anchored.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Moor means to secure a boat or ship in place with ropes, cables or an anchor. (लंगर डालना / बाँधना)

 

• "The boat was moored at the edge of the island" = the boat was anchored/tied up there.
◦  Hence 'Anchored' is the best replacement.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (Sailed): 'Sailed' means travelled on water — opposite in sense to being fixed in place.

 

• Option 3 (Lost): 'Lost' is unrelated.

 

• Option 4 (Floated): 'Floated' means drifted on water — not secured.

 

• Related nautical terms: berth (a ship's place in a port), dock, harbour, wharf, jetty.

 

NOTE

 

• Do not confuse 'moor' (to secure a boat; also an open upland area) with 'Moor' (historical term for North African Muslims).

question:

question: Which of the following options is NOT one of the meanings of the homonym 'compound'?
option_1: A substance formed from two or more elements chemically combined
option_2: A building or group of buildings enclosed by a barrier
option_3: To make something worse by adding to it
option_4: To subtract or reduce gradually over time
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. To subtract or reduce gradually over time.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Compound is a homonym with several meanings: (i) a substance formed by chemically combining two or more elements; (ii) an enclosed area containing buildings; (iii) (verb) to make a problem worse; (iv) (verb) to combine. (यौगिक / अहाता / बढ़ाना)

 

• 'To subtract or reduce gradually over time' is not a meaning of compound; in fact, 'compound interest' involves adding interest to the principal.
◦  Hence Option 4 is correct.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (A substance formed from two or more elements chemically combined): 'A substance formed from two or more elements chemically combined' — a valid meaning (chemistry: water is a compound).

 

• Option 2 (A building or group of buildings enclosed by a barrier): 'A building or group of buildings enclosed by a barrier' — a valid meaning (a school compound).

 

• Option 3 (To make something worse by adding to it): 'To make something worse by adding to it' — a valid meaning (His lies compounded the problem).

 

• Other uses: compound word (made of two words, e.g., toothpaste); compound interest.

 

NOTE

 

• Homonym questions test knowledge of multiple meanings of the same word.

question: Which of the following options is not one of the meanings of the homonym 'project'?
option_1: A planned piece of work to achieve a goal
option_2: To extend outward or stick out
option_3: A protective structure used in military defence
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. A protective structure used in military defence.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Project has these meanings: (noun) a planned piece of work; (verb) to extend outward/stick out; (verb) to estimate or forecast; (verb) to throw an image onto a screen. (परियोजना / उभरना / अनुमान लगाना)

 

• 'A protective structure used in military defence' is not a meaning of 'project' — such a structure is a rampart, bastion or bunker.
◦  Hence Option 3 is correct.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (A planned piece of work to achieve a goal): 'A planned piece of work to achieve a goal' — a valid meaning (a science project).

 

• Option 2 (To extend outward or stick out): 'To extend outward or stick out' — a valid meaning (The balcony projects over the street).

 

• Option 4 (To guess or estimate something): 'To guess or estimate something' — a valid meaning (projected sales figures).

 

• Stress shift: PROject (noun) vs proJECT (verb) — a common heteronym pattern (REcord/reCORD, PREsent/preSENT).

 

NOTE

 

• Military defence structures: rampart, bastion, bunker, parapet, fortification.

question:

• 'assail' (attack), 'assailant' (attacker).

question:
The following sentence has been divided into four parts, namely A, B, C and D, which are given in the alternatives. Select the alternative that contains the part of the sentence with an error.

The child requested his mother to gave him a big chocolate because he had been very good all day long and deserved a treat.
option_1: The child requested his mother to
option_2: gave him a big chocolate because he
option_3: had been very good all day
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. gave him a big chocolate because he.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The verb request follows the pattern request + object + to-infinitive (to + V1). 'to gave' is wrong; it should be 'to give'. (to + V1)

 

• Correct: "The child requested his mother to give him a big chocolate because he had been very good all day long and deserved a treat."
◦  Hence the error is in part B.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (The child requested his mother to): 'The child requested his mother to' is correct.

 

• Option 3 (had been very good all day): 'had been very good all day' is correct past perfect (earlier than 'requested').

 

• Option 4 (long and deserved a treat): 'long and deserved a treat.' is correct; 'all day long' is an idiom.

 

• Rule: 'to' + base form of verb (infinitive) — never 'to + V2'.

 

NOTE

 

• Verbs followed by object + to-infinitive: request, ask, tell, advise, order, allow, want, expect.

question:
Arrange the following sentences in the correct order to form a logically sound and coherent paragraph.

The parts are:

A. joke and endeavoured to smile appropriately, though

B. to say shock, remained detectable in my expression.

C. I suspect some residue of my bewilderment, not

D. Then I realized he was making some sort of
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. DACB.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• D 'Then I realized he was making some sort of' opens the sentence, and A 'joke and endeavoured to smile appropriately, though' completes 'some sort of joke'. (वाक्य संरचना)

 

• C 'I suspect some residue of my bewilderment, not' follows 'though', and B 'to say shock, remained detectable in my expression.' ends it ('not to say shock').
◦  Sequence: DACB.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (DCBA): 'some sort of I suspect' is meaningless.

 

• Option 2 (DBCA): 'some sort of to say shock' is meaningless.

 

• Option 3 (DABC): 'though to say shock' breaks the phrase 'not to say'.

 

• 'Not to say' = introducing a stronger alternative: It was difficult, not to say impossible.

 

NOTE

 

• Noun phrases broken across parts ('some sort of' + 'joke') help fix the order.

question:
From the given alternatives, select the correct indirect narration of the given direct narration.

Pari said to Nirvaan, "He admitted that he had made a huge mistake in judgment when he decided to invest all his money in that risky startup company."
option_1: Pari told Nirvaan that he had admitted that he had made a huge mistake in judgment when he decided to invest all his money in that risky startup company.
option_2: Pari told Nirvaan that he admitted that he had made a huge mistake in judgment when he decided to invest all his money in that risky startup company.
option_3: Pari told Nirvaan that he had admitted that he made a huge mistake in judgment when he decided to invest all his money in that risky startup company.
option_4: Pari told Nirvaan that he had admitted that he had made a huge mistake in judgment when he decided to invested all his money in that risky startup company.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Pari told Nirvaan that he had admitted that he had made a huge mistake in judgment when he decided to invest all his money in that risky startup company.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The reporting verb 'said to' → told. The reported speech 'He admitted' (simple past) → 'had admitted' (past perfect). The clause 'he had made' is already past perfect and stays unchanged; 'when he decided' (time clause) usually stays in simple past. (अप्रत्यक्ष कथन)

 

• Indirect: "Pari told Nirvaan that he had admitted that he had made a huge mistake in judgment when he decided to invest all his money in that risky startup company."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (Pari told Nirvaan that he admitted that he had made a huge mistake in judgment when he decided to invest all his money in that risky startup company): 'he admitted' is not backshifted to past perfect.

 

• Option 3 (Pari told Nirvaan that he had admitted that he made a huge mistake in judgment when he decided to invest all his money in that risky startup company): 'he made' wrongly changes the existing past perfect 'had made' to simple past.

 

• Option 4 (Pari told Nirvaan that he had admitted that he had made a huge mistake in judgment when he decided to invested all his money in that risky startup company): 'to invested' is ungrammatical; the infinitive is 'to invest'.

 

• Rule: Past perfect in direct speech remains past perfect in indirect speech.

 

NOTE

 

• Past simple in time clauses (when he decided) is often left unchanged to avoid awkward repetition of 'had'.

question:
From the given alternatives, select the correct indirect narration of the given direct narration.

Sarthak said to Reyansh, "I believe that every single person deserves a second chance to make things right after making a mistake."
option_1: Sarthak told Reyansh that he had believed that every single person deserved a second chance to make things right after making a mistake.
option_2: Sarthak told Reyansh that he believes that every single person deserved a second chance to make things right after making a mistake.
option_3: Sarthak told Reyansh that he believed that every single person deserving a second chance to make things right after making a mistake.
option_4: Sarthak told Reyansh that he believed that every single person deserved a second chance to make things right after making a mistake.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Sarthak told Reyansh that he believed that every single person deserved a second chance to make things right after making a mistake.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• With the past reporting verb: 'said to' → told; I → he; believe → believed; deserves → deserved. (अप्रत्यक्ष कथन)

 

• Indirect: "Sarthak told Reyansh that he believed that every single person deserved a second chance to make things right after making a mistake."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (Sarthak told Reyansh that he had believed that every single person deserved a second chance to make things right after making a mistake): 'had believed' — simple present should become simple past, not past perfect.

 

• Option 2 (Sarthak told Reyansh that he believes that every single person deserved a second chance to make things right after making a mistake): 'believes' is not backshifted.

 

• Option 3 (Sarthak told Reyansh that he believed that every single person deserving a second chance to make things right after making a mistake): 'deserving' leaves the clause without a finite verb — ungrammatical.

 

• Note: If the statement is treated as a general truth, the present tense may be retained — but here the options with mixed tenses (believes/deserved) are inconsistent, so full backshift is the answer.

 

NOTE

 

• Simple present → simple past (believe → believed; deserves → deserved).

question:
From the given alternatives, select the correct direct narration of the given indirect narration.

Sanvi told Prakash that the coach had announced that practice would be cancelled for the rest of the week due to the flooded condition of the playing fields.
option_1: Sanvi said to Prakash, "The coach is announcing that practice would be cancelled for the rest of the week due to the flooded condition of the playing fields."
option_2: Sanvi said to Prakash, "The coach announced that practice would have been cancelled for the rest of the week due to the flooded condition of the playing fields."
option_3: Sanvi said to Prakash, "The coach announced that practice would be cancelled for the rest of the week due to the flooded condition of the playing fields."
option_4: Sanvi said to Prakash, "The coach announced that practice would be cancelling for the rest of the week due to the flooded condition of the playing fields."
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Sanvi said to Prakash, "The coach announced that practice would be cancelled for the rest of the week due to the flooded condition of the playing fields."

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Reversing indirect to direct: 'told' → said to. The reported clause 'the coach had announced' (past perfect) → 'announced' (simple past). The inner clause 'practice would be cancelled' remains unchanged. (प्रत्यक्ष कथन)

 

• Direct: Sanvi said to Prakash, "The coach announced that practice would be cancelled for the rest of the week due to the flooded condition of the playing fields."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (Sanvi said to Prakash, "The coach is announcing that practice would be cancelled for the rest of the week due to the flooded condition of the playing fields."): 'is announcing' changes past perfect to present continuous — wrong reverse change.

 

• Option 2 (Sanvi said to Prakash, "The coach announced that practice would have been cancelled for the rest of the week due to the flooded condition of the playing fields."): 'would have been cancelled' alters the inner clause.

 

• Option 4 (Sanvi said to Prakash, "The coach announced that practice would be cancelling for the rest of the week due to the flooded condition of the playing fields."): 'would be cancelling' is active in form — practice cannot cancel itself; the passive 'be cancelled' is required.

 

• Reverse change: past perfect (indirect) → simple past or present perfect (direct).

 

NOTE

 

• Only the reporting layer is changed; embedded reported clauses already in the past generally remain as they are.

question:
From the given alternatives, select the correct direct narration of the given indirect narration.

Shivi told Rahul that he had realized that the mysterious footprints in the snow were actually made by a very large neighborhood dog.
option_1: Shivi said to Rahul, "He realized that the mysterious footprints in the snow were actually made by a very large neighborhood dog."
option_2: Shivi said to Rahul, "He realizes that the mysterious footprints in the snow were actually made by a very large neighborhood dog."
option_3: Shivi said to Rahul, "He realized that the mysterious footprints in the snow had been actually made by a very large neighborhood dog."
option_4: Shivi said to Rahul, "He realized that the mysterious footprints in the snow were actually made from a very large neighborhood dog."
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Shivi said to Rahul, "He realized that the mysterious footprints in the snow were actually made by a very large neighborhood dog."

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Reversing indirect to direct: 'told' → said to; 'he had realized' → 'He realized' (past perfect → simple past). The rest of the clause remains the same. (प्रत्यक्ष कथन)

 

• Direct: Shivi said to Rahul, "He realized that the mysterious footprints in the snow were actually made by a very large neighborhood dog."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (Shivi said to Rahul, "He realizes that the mysterious footprints in the snow were actually made by a very large neighborhood dog."): 'He realizes' changes it to present tense — incorrect.

 

• Option 3 (Shivi said to Rahul, "He realized that the mysterious footprints in the snow had been actually made by a very large neighborhood dog."): 'had been actually made' alters the inner clause unnecessarily.

 

• Option 4 (Shivi said to Rahul, "He realized that the mysterious footprints in the snow were actually made from a very large neighborhood dog."): 'made from a … dog' — the agent in passive takes 'by', not 'from'.

 

• Made by vs Made from/of: made by + doer (made by a carpenter); made from/of + material (made of wood, made from milk).

• 'He' refers to a third person, so it remains 'He' in direct speech.

question:
In the following sentence, a part of the sentence is bolded. Choose the correct alternative that best improves the bolded part.

The executive council has reached to a unanimous decision regarding the acquisition of the rival firm after months of negotiation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. has reached.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Reach is a transitive verb; it takes a direct object without 'to'. 'reached to a decision' is wrong. (पहुँचना – बिना 'to')

 

• The subject 'The executive council' is a collective noun acting as one body → singular verb has reached.
◦  Correct: "The executive council has reached a unanimous decision…"

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (have reached): 'have reached' — the council acts as a single unit here (a unanimous decision), so the singular 'has' is appropriate.

 

• Option 2 (reached to): 'reached to' retains the incorrect 'to'.

 

• Option 4 (reaching): 'reaching' leaves the sentence without a finite verb.

 

• Verbs that do not take 'to': reach, enter, discuss, resemble, attack, order, marry (enter into the room ✗, discuss about ✗).

 

NOTE

 

• 'Reach' can take 'to' only in the sense of extending: The curtains reach to the floor.

question:

solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. the more intelligent of the two.

• Correct: "She is considered the more intelligent of the two architects…"
◦  The superlative is used for three or more.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

• Option 3 (more intelligent than the two): 'more intelligent than the two' implies she is not one of the two — illogical.

 

• Option 4 (intelligent of the two): 'intelligent of the two' omits the comparative 'more'.

 

• Rule: the + comparative + of the two (the taller of the two brothers); the + superlative + of/in + group of three or more.

 

NOTE

 

• 'The' is used before the comparative in 'of the two' constructions and in 'the … the' structures (The more, the merrier).

question:
In the following sentence, a part of the sentence is bolded. Choose the correct alternative that best improves the bolded part.

I prefer to analyze the raw data personally to relying on the subjective interpretations provided by the junior researchers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. I prefer analyzing.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The verb prefer in the pattern 'prefer A to B' requires parallel forms. Since B is a gerund ('to relying'), A must also be a gerund: prefer analyzing … to relying. (prefer + V-ing … to + V-ing)

 

• Correct: "I prefer analyzing the raw data personally to relying on the subjective interpretations provided by the junior researchers."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (I prefer reading ... than): 'I prefer reading … than' — 'prefer' takes 'to', not 'than'; 'reading' also changes the meaning.

 

• Option 3 (I prefer to reading): 'I prefer to reading' — 'to + V-ing' after prefer is ungrammatical here.

 

• Option 4 (I prefer read): 'I prefer read' — 'prefer' is not followed by a bare infinitive.

 

• Patterns: prefer + V-ing + to + V-ing (I prefer walking to driving); prefer + to V1 + rather than + V1 (I prefer to walk rather than drive).

 

NOTE

 

• 'Prefer' is a Latin comparative — it takes 'to', never 'than' (like senior to, superior to).
